parole.significato: Used in the names of imageboards, usually ones that try to emulate 4chan.
parole.testo: In reference to 4chan, in turn from Futaba Channel (cf. its URL, www.2chan.net, or its alternate names ふたばちゃん and 双葉ちゃん found on its homepage); hence, derived from Japanese チャンネル (channeru), from English channel.

parole.significato: J-pop idol (popular performer in Japan)
parole.testo: From Japanese アイドル (aidoru), itself from English idol. Doublet of eidolon, idol, and idolum.

parole.significato: amateur sumo
parole.testo: From Japanese アマ相撲 (ama-sumō); ama is a shortening of English amateur.

parole.significato: An anime song; anime music.
parole.testo: From Japanese アニソン (anison), from アニ(メ) (anime) + ソン(グ) (songu), itself from English anime song. Equivalent to a blend of anime + song.

parole.significato: Synonym of water aerobics.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese アクアビクス (akuabikusu), from English aqua- + aerobics.

parole.significato: A flip-flop (footwear).
parole.testo: Calque of Japanese ビーチサンダル (bīchi sandaru), from English beach + sandal.

parole.significato: Figure-hugging, skintight, form-fitting.
parole.testo: From Japanese ボディコン (bodikon) (clipping of English body conscious), name of a fashion subculture among young Japanese women in the mid-to-late 1980s and early 1990s.

parole.significato: A representation of the sound of something bouncing.
parole.testo: Onomatopoeic. The “large breasts” sense is reborrowed from Japanese ボイン, in turn from English boing.

parole.significato: a genre of fictional media originating in Japan that features homoerotic relationships between male characters; yaoi
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ボーイズラブ (bōizu rabu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from boys + love.

parole.significato: Having large, well-developed muscles.
parole.testo: Reportedly coined in reference to the extremely muscular character Broly from the Dragon Ball anime franchise, with the suffix -ic. Broly is a transliteration of the Japanese ブロリー (Burorī), itself coined as a pun on the English broccoli, a theme used in the naming of members of the fictional Saiyan

parole.significato: Girls' used underwear and/or school uniforms, which are bought and sold by sexual fetishists.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese ブルセラ (burusera), from a combination of ブルマー (burumā, “bloomers”) + セーラー服 (sērā-fuku, “sailor suit”), from English bloomers and sailor respectively.

parole.significato: A type of hotel with a number of very small "rooms" (capsules).
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese カプセルホテル (kapuseru hoteru), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from capsule + hotel.

parole.significato: Synonym of virtual YouTuber.
parole.testo: From Japanese VTuber (bui-chūbā), from English virtual + YouTuber.

parole.significato: a form of Japanese pop music that emerged in the late 1970s and peaked in popularity during the 1980s, including influe…
parole.testo: From Japanese シティ・ポップ (shiti poppu), itself from English city pop.

parole.significato: Roux with curry powder.
parole.testo: Calque of Japanese カレールー (karē rū), from English curry and French roux.

parole.significato: Ornate decoration of phone cases, incorporating charms and sculpture.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese デコ電 (deko-den), from English decoration and Japanese 電話 (denwa, “telephone”).

parole.significato: A genre of Japanese big trucks, which are customized by their owner-operators into graphic and sculptural displays whic…
parole.testo: From Japanese dekotora (dekotora), from デコトラ, from デコ+トラ, from デコレーション (“dekorēshon (dekorēshon)”) + トラッ (“torakku (torakku)”), from English decorated + truck.

parole.significato: (A computer program that places) an interactive character on the desktop.
parole.termine_origine: デスクトップマスコット

catena.termine: デスクトップマスコット

parole.testo: Calque of Japanese デスクトップマスコット, from English desktop + mascot.

parole.significato: Tiles that provide bonus score multiplier points (飜 (han)) in a winning hand, indicated by one or multiple face-up tile…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese ドラ (dora), a clipping of Japanese ドラゴン (doragon), from English dragon.

parole.significato: Japanese TV drama.
parole.testo: From Japanese ドラマ (dorama), from English drama.

parole.significato: To remove (a feature, subplot, item, or character) from a video game.
parole.testo: From Japanese ダミー (damī), which was often used as a placeholder term for the designation of certain things that ended up going unused in a video game. The Japanese term was itself derived from English dummy, and thus tended to be translated in games (even if inaccessible by normal means) as "DUMMY".

parole.significato: waste bin, trash can
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ダストボックス (dasutobokkusu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from dust + box.

parole.significato: Of animation, erotic, lascivious, lewd, naughty, sexy, suggestive.
parole.testo: From Japanese エッチ (etchi, “dirty; perverted”), which is derived from English aitch (“name of the letter ⟨H⟩”), which is an initialism of the romaji of Japanese 変(へん)態(たい) (hentai, “pervert”). エッチ (etchi) is not a genre in Japanese; this is a development in English (pseudo-Japonism), similar to that

parole.significato: A style of lure fishing specifically targeting squid (and occasionally cuttlefish) using a specialized wooden or plasti…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese エギング (egingu), a Wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism), derived from 餌木 (egi) + -ing.

parole.significato: A Japanese literary and artistic movement of the 1920s and 1930s, focusing on eroticism, sexual corruption and decadenc…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese エログロ (eroguro), ultimately from English erotic + grotesque.

parole.significato: A visual novel with erotic content.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese エロゲ (eroge) (less commonly エロゲー (erogē)), a shortening of エロチックゲーム (erochikku gēmu), from English erotic game.

parole.significato: A short scene or illustration used to begin and end a commercial break in a Japanese television program.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese アイキャッチ (aikyatchi), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from eye + catch.

parole.significato: A Japanese fashion style influenced by pop culture of the 1980s, characterized by pastel colours and whimsical, childli…
parole.testo: From Japanese フェアリー系 (fearī-kei, literally “fairy style”), from フェアリー (fearī, “fairy”) (itself from English fairy) + 系 (kei, “style”).

parole.significato: A Family Computer (chiefly those available within Japan).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese ファミコン (famikon), a syllabic abbreviation of ファミリーコンピューター (famirīkonpyūtā), a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from family + computer.

parole.significato: Elements added to a television program or similar entertainment that appeal to avid fans but are of little interest to…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ファンサービス (fansābisu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from fan + service.

parole.significato: In Japan, a young person (typically between the ages of 15-34) who lacks full-time employment (excluding housewives and…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese フリーター (furītā), possibly from English free and German Arbeiter (“labourer”).

parole.significato: Synonym of brush pen.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese 筆ペン (fudepen), a compound of 筆 (fude, “brush”) and ペン (pen, from English pen).

parole.significato: A video game centered around interactions with attractive anime-style girls.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese ギャルゲー (gyarugē), a shortening of ギャルゲーム (gyaru gēmu), a wasei-eigo derived from English gal + game.

parole.significato: game over
parole.testo: Calque of Japanese ゲームセット (gēmu setto), derived from English game, set, match.

parole.significato: A genre of Japanese media focusing on romantic and/or sexual relationships between female characters.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ガールズラブ (gāruzu rabu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from girls + love.

parole.significato: A Japanese fashion movement whose adherents dress in an elegant, largely monochromatic style with traditional accoutrem…
parole.testo: From Japanese ゴスロリ (gosurori), a blend of ゴス (Goth, “Goth”) + ロリータ (lolita), from English lolita.

parole.significato: A female pin-up model from Japanese erotica
parole.testo: gravure + idol. From Japanese グラビアアイドル (gravure idol, “gurabia aidoru”), from グラビア (“gurabia”) + アイドル (“aidoru”), from English gravure (“engraving”)+idol

parole.significato: A subgenre of manga and anime focusing on gore and mutilation.
parole.testo: Reborrowed from Japanese グロ (guro), from English grotesque.

parole.significato: A Japanese subculture and fashion style popular in the 1990s, typically involving ostentatious clothing, tanning, and h…
parole.testo: From Japanese ギャル (gyaru), from English gal, from English girl.

parole.significato: Pornographic in a way characteristic of hentai.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese H, alternative form of エッチ (etchi), in turn from English H as an abbreviation of Japanese 変態 (hentai, “pervert”). A doublet of ecchi (“erotic, lascivious”) and hentai (“pornographic anime, manga, etc.”).

parole.significato: person of half or mixed ethnic Japanese and other ancestries usually from outside Japan
parole.testo: From Japanese ハーフ (hāfu, “mixed-race (unspecified)”), from English half. Doublet of half.

parole.significato: Synonym of freeze pop, frozen fruit juice or flavored ice in a tube.
parole.testo: Calque of Japanese アイスキャンディー (aisukyandī, literally “ice candy”), a Wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism), derived from ice + candy.

parole.significato: A handbag, backpack, or other bag decorated with fandom-related merchandise such as pins, badges, and dolls (typically…
parole.testo: From Japanese 痛バッグ (ita baggu, “painful bag”), from 痛 (ita, “pain”) + バッグ (baggu, “bag”), itself from English bag.

parole.significato: Japanese pop music influenced by Western genres.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese J-POP (jeipoppu), from J- + pop, an abbreviation of English Japanese pop, coined by Tokyo radio station J‑WAVE in 1988.

parole.significato: A type of number puzzle, similar to a crossword but with numbers. Each "clue" is the sum of the digits to be placed in…
parole.testo: From Japanese カックロ (kakkuro), in turn derived from English Cross Sums.

parole.significato: Panko breaded and deep-fried Japanese food
parole.testo: From Japanese カツ (katsu, “cutlet”), shortening of カツレツ (katsuretsu), itself from English cutlet. Thus a doublet of English cut.

parole.significato: A hybrid martial art derived from Muay Thai, karate, and especially boxing during the 1960s to 1970s; more generally, a…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese キックボクシング (kikkubokushingu), from English kick + boxing. Possibly coined by Japanese businessman Osamu Noguchi in 1964.

parole.significato: A subculture of conspicuous consumption among young women in urban Japan, typified by dyed hair, artificial suntan, pla…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese コギャル (kogyaru, “younger gyaru”) (see there for more), ultimately from English gal.

parole.significato: kogal
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese コギャル (“younger gyaru”), ultimately from English gal, a dialectal pronunciation of English girl.

parole.significato: A calm, aloof, reserved fictional character (usually a girl) who has a hidden soft side, especially for a love interest.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese クーデレ (kūdere), a portmanteau of クール (kūru, “calm”), from English cool, and デレデレ (dere-dere, “in a lovey-dovey, infatuated, or lovestruck manner”, adverb).

parole.significato: A kind of Japanese club where hostesses are paid to entertain and drink and talk with customers.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese キャバクラ, itself from English cabaret club.

parole.significato: A style of elaborately arranged bento which features food decorated to look like people, characters from popular media,…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese キャラ弁 (kyaraben), a contraction of キャラクター弁当 (kyarakutā bentō), itself from English character and Japanese 弁当 (bentō).

parole.significato: A Japanese novel primarily targeting young adults, typically illustrated (in an anime/manga style) and containing not m…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ライトノベル (raito noberu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from light + novel.

parole.significato: A childlike female character, particularly in the lolicon genre.
parole.testo: From Japanese ロリ (rori), itself from English lolita or a clipping of lolicon.

parole.significato: A fashion style originating in Japan, based on Victorian and Edwardian clothing styles, and having a cute aesthetic.
parole.termine_origine: ロリータファッション

catena.termine: ロリータファッション

parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ロリータファッション (rorīta fasshon), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from Lolita + fashion.

parole.significato: A short-stay hotel found in Japan and elsewhere, operated primarily for the purpose of allowing lovers privacy to have…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ラブホテル (rabu hoteru), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from love + hotel. The term probably makes reference to the rotating sign of the Hotel Love, an early love hotel in Osaka, Japan.

parole.significato: A style of light-tackle saltwater angling originating in Japan, specifically targeting rockfish using small artificial…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese メバリング (mebaringu), a Wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism), derived from 鮴 (mebaru) + -ing.

parole.significato: A large armoured robot on legs, typically controlled by a pilot seated inside.
parole.testo: From Japanese メカ (meka), from an abbreviation of the English mechanical.

parole.significato: A female fictional character who is employed as a maid, typically wearing a stylized French maid outfit.
parole.testo: From Japanese メイド (meido, “maid, maidservant”), from English maid.

parole.significato: A kind of Japanese visual novel featuring moe content, including cute characters and art style.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese 萌(も)えゲー (moegē), a combination of 萌(も)え (moe, “moe”) and ゲー (gē), a shortening of ゲーム (gēmu, “game”), itself from English game.

parole.significato: An apron worn over a person's naked body.
parole.testo: A calque of Japanese 裸エプロン (はだかエプロン, hadaka epuron), from 裸 (はだか, hadaka, “naked, nude, bare”) + エプロン (epuron, “apron”), in turn borrowed from English apron.

parole.significato: A Japanese visual novel of a genre characterized by melodramatic plots intended to move the player to tears.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese 泣きゲー (nakige, “crying game”), a compound of なき (naki, “crying”) and ゲー (gē), a shortening of ゲーム (gēmu, “game”), itself from English game. Compare tearjerker.

parole.significato: A Japanese visual novel genre featuring sexually explicit content for the sole purpose of masturbation or sexual gratif…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese 抜(ぬ)きゲー (nukigē), a combination of 抜(ぬ)く (nuku, “to jerk off”, literally “to extract”) and ゲー (gē), a shortening of ゲーム (gēmu, “game”), itself from English game.

parole.significato: The instrumentals.
parole.testo: From Japanese オフボーカル (ofubōkaru), from English off + vocal.

parole.significato: upskirt, panty shot
parole.testo: From Japanese パンチラ, itself from English panty.

parole.significato: panties (short underpants for women or girls); underpants
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese パンツ (pantsu), from English pants.

parole.significato: A person who has a driver's license but never drives.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese ペーパードライバー (pēpā doraibā), from English paper + driver.

parole.significato: A pierced earring.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese ピアス (piasu, “pierced earring”), itself from English pierce.

parole.significato: A fictional creature from the universe of the Pokémon franchise.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese ポケットモンスター (Poketto Monsutā), itself from English pocket + monster.

parole.significato: A place believed to contain sacred power.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese パワースポット (pawā supotto), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from power + spot.

parole.significato: A collectable item that gives the player some benefit.
parole.testo: Calque of Japanese パワーアップ (pawā-appu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from power + up.

parole.significato: Japanese professional wrestling
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese プロレス (puroresu), an abbreviation of プロフェッショナル・レスリング (purofesshonaru resuringu), itself borrowed from English professional wrestling.

parole.significato: A secondhand shop.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese リサイクルショップ (risaikuru shoppu), from English recycle + shop.

parole.significato: A win in a fighting game obtained by throwing one's opponent out of the arena.
parole.testo: Calque of Japanese リングアウト (ringu auto), equivalent to English ring (noun) + out (verb)

parole.significato: A school uniform commonly worn by girls in Japan, based on the traditional sailor suit but with a pleated skirt.
parole.testo: Partial calque from Japanese セーラー服(ふく) (sērāfuku, literally “sailor outfit”), from セーラー (sērā, “sailor”) (from English sailor) + 服(ふく) (-fuku, “clothes”).

parole.significato: An employee, a worker; now especially a Japanese white-collar worker who works long hours yet has an insignificant posi…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese サラリーマン (sararīman), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from salary + man.

parole.significato: A Japanese-style sandwich with crustless white bread and sometimes a sweet filling.
parole.testo: From Japanese サンド (sando), a shortening from English sandwich.

parole.significato: thank you
parole.testo: From Japanese サンキュー (sankyū), from English thank you.

parole.significato: striped panties
parole.testo: From Japanese しまパン, itself from English panty.

parole.significato: The best moment to take a picture of a moving subject.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese シャッターチャンス (shattā chansu), from English shutter + chance.

parole.significato: Bonding through physical (touch, skin-to-skin) contact; particularly between family members, relatives and loved ones.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese スキンシップ (sukinshippu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from English skin + -ship, or as a blend from English skin + kinship. It is first recorded in English in 1966 according to the OED. In Japanese, this form was also observed in the Latin scr

parole.significato: A variant of tennis, developed in Japan, differing in the tennis ball used, from regular tennis (lawn tennis), having a…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese ソフトテニス (sofuto tenisu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from soft + tenis.

parole.significato: A makeup special effects technique for portraying enormous creatures, by having an actor wear a suit near a set of mina…
parole.testo: From Japanese スーツメーション, from blend of English suit + English animation. Originally used to describe the technique used on Gojira (Godzilla) to make the creature come to life.

parole.significato: A superchat.
parole.testo: From some form of Japanese スーパーチャット (sūpā chatto, “superchat”), from English superchat.

parole.significato: A video game genre that emphasizes scarcity of resources (such as health or ammunition refills) in a dangerous setting…
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Japanese サバイバルホラー (sabaibaru horā), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from survival + horror.

parole.significato: A Japanese fashion movement whose adherents dress in pastel colours and styles resembling clothing for young girls.
parole.testo: From Japanese 甘ロリ (amarori), a blend of 甘い (amai, “sweet, sugary”) + ロリータ (lolita), from English lolita.

parole.significato: A yoshoku dish from Okinawa, mainly consisting of ground beef on a bed of rice.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching from Japanese タコライス (takoraisu), itself a wasei eigo (和製英語; pseudo-anglicism) derived from taco + rice.

parole.significato: A toy consisting of a small electronic virtual pet, a cyberpet.
parole.testo: A genericization of Tamagotchi, the name of a virtual pet series: the word is a Japanese blend of 卵 (たまご, tamago, “egg”) + ウオッチ (uotchi, from English watch).

parole.significato: A celebrity who regularly appears on mass media in Japan, especially as a panelist on variety shows.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese タレント (tarento, “television star”), from English talent. Doublet of talent.

parole.significato: An attack in which one may gain an advantage in time against one's opponent or rival.
parole.testo: From time + attack. The time-trial sense is a calque of Japanese タイムアタック (taimu atakku), itself from English.

parole.significato: An early type of video game, the predecessor of modern games consoles, consisting of a unit with a built-in controller…
parole.testo: NNSE sense is borrowed from Japanese テレビゲーム (terebi gēmu), from English TV + game.

parole.significato: A Japanese visual novel genre characterized by tragic plots and pervasively bleak tones.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese 鬱ゲー (utsuge, “depressing game”), a combination of 鬱 (utsu, “melancholy, gloom”) and ゲー (gē), a shortening of ゲーム (gēmu, “game”), itself from English game.

parole.significato: A Japanese music and fashion movement that emerged in the 1980s, characterized by a bold, extravagant, androgynous styl…
parole.testo: From Japanese ヴィジュアル系(けい) (vijuaru-kei, literally “visual style”), composed of ヴィジュアル (vijuaru, “visual”), itself from English visual, and 系 (kei, “style”).

parole.significato: An interactive fiction video game of a style originated in Japan, consisting primarily of narration illustrated by anim…
parole.testo: Calque of Japanese ビジュアルノベル (bijuaru noberu), from English visual + novel.

parole.significato: An artificial singer (a voicebank, usually with an avatar) based on the Vocaloid engine.
parole.testo: From Vocaloid, from Japanese VOCALOID(ボーカロイド) (bōkaroido), from English vocal + -oid.

parole.significato: A yellow taxi, particularly officially licensed taxis in New York City and certain other jurisdictions.
parole.testo: Originally selected owing to yellow's high visibility and common in horsedrawn form in Paris and London in the 1800s and New York in the 1880s. Now chiefly associated with the yellow automotive taxicabs popularized around New York by the Yellow Taxicab Co. In reference to sexually available Asian wo

parole.significato: Application of financial engineering techniques in Japanese financial markets since their deregulation in 1984.
parole.testo: From Japanese 財テク (zaiteku, “money management”), from blend of 財務 (zaimu, “financial dealings”) and テクノロジー (tekunorojii, “technology”), the latter, from English technology. The -tech in zaitech reflects the original borrowing of English technology.
